text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament's speaker Blagovest Sendov said he will decide on Monday whether to convene delegates for an extraordinary session to vote on Prime Minister's Zhan Videnov's resignation. The resignation can be submitted to parliament on Friday, when parliament's office will open after the Christmas holiday.
- The president of the Slavia soccer club Lyubcho Vasilev has been arrested on allegations of racketeering, said Bulgarian Soccer Federation sources.
- Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev and Foreign Minister Georgi Pirinski, who resigned last month, have the biggest chances to replace Prime Minister Zhan Videnov.
- The International Monetary Fund has recommended a lev/dollar rate of 600 for 1997. Annual inflation in yet another draft budget for next year is projected at 72 percent.

- The Construction Ministry is expected to sell 45 firms for 5.5 billion levs nex year, a ministry official has said. The biggest are three cement plants: Zlatna Panega, Beloisvorski Cement and Granitoid.
- Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev demanded change in the government. The cabinet had failed to deal with corruption, Dobrev told the Bulgarian Socialist Party congress.
- The chief economist of the Bulgarian National Bank and board member, Lena Rousenova, has tendered her resignation, bank sources said.
- Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's resignation has not yet been deposited in parliament, said the speaker's secretary
